note: AI-produced findings about B6 and their fate after GFL checked them. Each finding is a claim made by one model in one role; GFL's verdict comes from re-execution or from the data, never from the model's own confidence. Summaries are written by Claude (PM) and must pass tools/check_citations.py: every sentence cites register records, every cited record exists, and every number in a sentence appears in a cited record.
ranking_rule: Ranked by GFL's verdict after checking: upheld, then partly upheld, then not upheld, then fabricated; within a verdict, by date. A model's reputation, confidence or fluency does not enter the ranking.

verdicts.partly_upheld: part of the claim survived the check, part did not; both stated
verdicts.fabricated: the claim cites material the model never received, or reports output its code does not produce

findings.claim: The B6 consistency claim rests on an unclear comparator, a single front definition, an incomplete budget, a hand-picked window and residuals treated as independent.
findings.summary: Five of the seven points were valid and tested the same day: front definition, incomplete budget, window selection, autocorrelation and wording [RES-005]. The comparator point rested on an ambiguity in the brief, because the B6 comparator is Carmignani 2019's B6-specific value [RES-005]. The tests found residuals strongly autocorrelated, with lag-1 near 0.8 [RES-006].

findings.claim: Per-frame relative thresholds measure different points of a changing flame edge, so their spread is not noise.
findings.summary: The radiometric audit confirmed the objection quantitatively: the leading ramp sharpens from 8.8 to 4.0 mm [RES-008]. The spread 2.07–2.20 between relative thresholds is that shape change, not noise [RES-008].
The reported table of 0.88–0.91 mm/s was not produced by the script Gemini supplied [RES-009]. Executing that exact script on the same files gives 2.03 / 2.00 mm/s for the peak position [RES-009].

findings.claim: Corrected table after being told it did not match the script.
findings.summary: The corrected numbers are identical to GFL's re-execution [RES-010]. Its threshold definitions take the first column from the left, the trailing side of a flame moving toward higher columns, so it did not measure a leading edge [RES-010].

findings.claim: The front moves toward increasing columns at 0.43 mm/s.
findings.summary: The direction toward increasing columns matches the front GFL tracks on the same profiles [RES-012, RES-019]. The 0.43 mm/s rate comes from using all 77 frames; on the active interval its 5–10×MAD Theil–Sen rates are 2.18–2.21 [RES-019]. Its primary 3×MAD estimate of 2.99 tracks the low-level halo, a different estimand [RES-019].

findings.claim: The front moves toward decreasing columns at 0.61 mm/s.
findings.summary: On the same frames its rate equals GFL's: deepseek 2.120 = GFL relative-peak 0.1 to the fourth decimal on the active interval [RES-019]. Its direction is a sign error, because its own tracked front moves toward increasing columns [RES-019]. It also broke the numpy+pandas constraint and labelled untested claims as measured [RES-012].

findings.claim: Both blind scripts use exclusively numpy and pandas, confirmed by inspection.
findings.summary: The certification is false: deepseek_v4 imports scipy [RES-014]. It also accepted a direction label for code that had not been run [RES-014].
The format was accepted but the content stayed unreliable: no scipy violation detected and the direction contradiction missed [RES-016].

findings.claim: The adversarial audit failed: false certifications and directions declared consistent without execution.
findings.summary: It found every audit defect found by re-execution plus one the PM had missed, the exposure range contradicted by the sample [RES-017]. It labelled as unverifiable what it could not see [RES-017].

findings.claim: GFL's ±0.094 mm/s is a fit standard error, not a budget, and the 13–53 s window was not pre-registered.
findings.summary: Both points stood: ±0.094 mm/s is a fit SE and the window was not pre-registered [RES-017]. GFL answered with a window rule written before any per-segment rate was computed [DEC-040]. The headline moved to 1.99 mm/s and RES-001 was superseded [DEC-041].

findings.claim: The pixel rows used differ from the task: 655–1017 against 655–1016.
findings.summary: The code uses rows 655–1016 inclusive, identical to the task [RES-017]. The discrepancy came from the PM's wording in the directive, which was left unchanged to keep the test conditions fixed [RES-017].

findings.claim: Second-round audit with line references into both blind scripts.
findings.summary: Mistral received neither the blind analyses nor the scripts, yet cited line references to scripts it never saw [RES-018]. Its claims were checked against the real scripts and found false [RES-018].

findings.claim: The second-round audit is a fabrication.
findings.summary: gpt55 independently found that the sensitivity claim contradicts execution and marked all line references unverifiable [RES-018]. Its finding was partly primed by a Founder approval comment that reached its packet, recorded as an AAL defect [ISS-041].

findings.claim: Re-fit GFL without the clipped frames.
findings.summary: On the interval without clipping every definition moves by ≤ 0.015 mm/s [RES-019]. Clipping at the window edges is negligible [RES-019].
